name: Apple Screen Time (with Focus, Sleep Focus and Notification Summary)
purpose: A tool built into iPhone, iPad and Mac that shows how much time you spend on apps and lets you set when apps are available, daily time allowances and who can contact you.
keyFeatures: Usage reports: daily and weekly screen time, most-used apps, pickups and notifications
Screen Time Schedules (called Downtime on iOS 26 and earlier): choose when apps are available, e.g. bedtime
Time Allowances (called App Limits on iOS 26 and earlier): daily time for categories such as Games or Social Media
Communication Limits and Always Allowed: choose who can call or message you and which apps and contacts always work
Focus modes, including Sleep Focus, plus Scheduled Summary to bundle notifications at set times
costDetail: No separate price. It is part of iOS, iPadOS and macOS on Apple devices, and the Apple pages checked list no cost. The newest Screen Time features (Screen Time Schedules, Time Allowances, Share Across Devices) need iOS 27, iPadOS 27 or macOS 27 or later on all your devices. The basic Scheduled Summary for notifications is described with no device restriction. Apple Intelligence notification summaries and Priority Notifications need an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later) and are not available in all languages and regions.
accountRequired: Optional. An Apple Account is needed to sync Screen Time across iPhone, iPad and Mac (Share Across Devices), and Family Sharing with a Child Account is needed to manage a child's device. Apple's guide does not say an account is needed for basic use on one device.
privacyNotes: Reports cover which apps and websites you use, for how long, pickups and notifications. In Apple's iCloud data security overview, Screen Time data is listed as end-to-end encrypted under both Standard and Advanced Data Protection.
accessibilityNotes: No accessibility statement specific to Screen Time was found. It lives in Settings and System Settings, and iPhone, iPad and Mac include Apple's built-in VoiceOver screen reader.
limitations: Apple's iOS 26 guide says that by default Screen Time limits can be ignored once reached. Blocking them properly needs a Screen Time passcode and the Block at Downtime setting.
Only works on Apple devices. The latest Schedules and Time Allowances features need version 27 software on every device.
Feature names changed in iOS 27 (Downtime became Screen Time Schedules, App Limits became Time Allowances), so older tutorials may not match newer devices.

name: Google Digital Wellbeing
purpose: A section in the Settings of many Android phones that shows your phone habits and lets you set app timers, a Bedtime mode and a Focus mode.
keyFeatures: Dashboard of screen time per app, unlocks and notifications received
App timers: daily limits per app (the app closes and its icon dims when time runs out)
Bedtime mode: schedule or turn on while charging, with grayscale, dark screen, dimmed wallpaper and Do Not Disturb
Focus mode: pause chosen apps and their notifications, on a schedule or on demand
Website time limits for sites visited in Chrome, and an optional App limits PIN
costDetail: No price. It is reached from the phone's Settings app. Its Google Play listing (developer Google LLC) shows Install with no in-app purchases or ads listed. Google says it is available 'on some phones' and steps vary by device.
accountRequired: No account is mentioned for personal use. Google's help page describes it as part of Settings, where you set up a profile the first time. Parents can manage a child's device through Family Link.
privacyNotes: The Google Play Data safety section says 'No data shared with third parties' and that the app may collect 'Personal info, App activity and 3 others'. Data is encrypted in transit, and the listing says 'Data can’t be deleted'.
accessibilityNotes: No accessibility statement specific to Digital Wellbeing was found. Android includes Google's TalkBack screen reader, and Bedtime mode offers grayscale and dark theme options.
limitations: Only available 'on some phones', and steps vary by device maker
App timers reset at midnight and you can delete them yourself unless an App limits PIN is set. Some work and school accounts might not work with app timers.
Website time limits only cover browsing in Chrome

name: Forest: Focus for Productivity
purpose: A focus timer that grows a virtual tree while you stay off your phone. If you leave to use other apps, the tree dies.
keyFeatures: Focus timer (countdown and stopwatch) that grows a tree
Deep Focus app blocking during sessions (free on every tier)
Time Guard scheduled app and site blocks (1 app or site free, several with Plus)
Plant Together group focus rooms with friends
Real trees planted with partner Trees for the Future (planting with coins is a Plus feature, up to 5 trees)
costDetail: Free to download on iOS ('Free · In-App Purchases') and Android ('Contains ads · In-app purchases'). The free tier includes the focus timer, Deep Focus app blocking, Time Guard for 1 app or site, focus tracking and Plant Together, and shows occasional ads (never during active focus sessions). The optional Forest Plus subscription (free trial available) adds a custom app allowlist, multi-app Time Guard, Focus Analytics, pausing sessions, all soundscapes, real-tree planting and no ads. Forest says 'Plus pricing varies by region and platform.' The US App Store lists 'Annual (Early Bird) $35.99' and 'Monthly (Early Bird) $5.99' (USD). Google Play shows in-app items at '$0.99 - $59.99 per item'. The old one-time Forest Pro purchase is no longer sold. The Chrome and Firefox extensions install at no cost. Core blocking is free, so essential features do not require payment.
accountRequired: Optional or unclear. An account syncs your forest and focus history across iPhone, iPad, Android and browser. Plant Together, Focus Challenge, the shop and real-tree planting need internet. Forest does not say whether sign-in is required for basic use.
privacyNotes: Forest says session data is stored with your account and not sold to third parties. The App Store privacy label lists Contact Info and Usage Data as 'Data Used to Track You'. Google Play says the app may share Personal info with third parties. The Chrome Web Store listing says the developer will not collect or use your data.
accessibilityNotes: The App Store listing says: 'The developer has not yet indicated which accessibility features this app supports.' No official accessibility statement was found.
limitations: The free tier shows ads (not during focus sessions). Pausing a session, Focus Analytics and multi-app Time Guard need Plus.
It is mainly a phone app. The browser extension only brings Deep Focus and the timer to desktop browsing, and no desktop app was found.
Plus prices vary by store and region, and the US App Store prices are labelled 'Early Bird', so the standard price is unclear.

name: Freedom
purpose: Blocks distracting apps and websites, or the whole internet, on your phone and computer at the same time.
keyFeatures: Block apps, websites or the entire internet
One block session synced across unlimited devices
Custom blocklists and focus sounds
Premium: scheduled and recurring sessions, and sessions planned for later in the day
Premium: Locked Mode (can't quit a session) and sessions longer than 2 hours
costDetail: The Free plan (US$0) lets you block apps, websites or the whole internet on unlimited devices. Free accounts are limited to 'Start Now' sessions and cannot run sessions longer than 2 hours, recurring sessions, Start Later sessions or Locked Mode. Premium costs US$8.99/month billed monthly, or US$3.33/month on the yearly plan ('Yearly - Save 40%'; the page does not print the annual total), with 'Try It Free For 7 Days'. A one-time 'Forever' plan is US$99.50, shown as 50% off US$199. Prices are 'plus tax where applicable'. In-app prices on the iOS App Store differ: 'Freedom Yearly Subscription $39.99', 'Freedom Yearly $59.99', 'Freedom Monthly $12.99', 'Freedom Forever $199.00'. Scheduling and Locked Mode, which help you stick to limits, require payment.
accountRequired: Yes. The install steps say to 'Launch and log in', and you sign up with your name, email and password.
privacyNotes: Freedom's FAQ says: 'Freedom doesn’t track your browsing, app usage, or personal activity.' However, the iOS App Store privacy label lists Identifiers under 'Data Used to Track You', and email address and user content as linked to you.
accessibilityNotes: The App Store listing says: 'The developer has not yet indicated which accessibility features this app supports.' No official accessibility statement was found.
limitations: Free sessions are 'Start Now' only and capped at 2 hours. There is no scheduling or Locked Mode without Premium.
Website exceptions are not available on iOS or Android. On Chromebook and Linux, Freedom only blocks websites through a browser extension (no app blocking).
Requires an account, and prices differ between the website and the App Store.

name: Cold Turkey Blocker
purpose: A strict blocker for Windows and Mac computers that blocks distracting websites (and, with Pro, apps) and is very hard to switch off once a block is locked.
keyFeatures: Block websites, with exceptions (free)
Timed blocks and usage statistics (free)
Pro: block apps and games, scheduled weekly blocks, and breaks and allowances
Pro: application password and 'All locking features', which make blocks hard to stop
Can block YouTube channels, keyword searches or the entire internet (the pricing page doesn't say whether these are Free or Pro)
costDetail: Blocker Free covers blocking websites, website exceptions, timed blocks and statistics, and includes a 7-day free trial of Pro. Blocker Pro is a one-time purchase ('Pay once, own forever') that covers all computers you personally use, with free lifetime updates, a 30-day money-back guarantee and 20% off for students on request. The price is not in the pricing page's HTML. The page loads it from Paddle (its merchant of record), which returned US$45.00 one-time (US) and ₹2,499 (India) on 2026-11-11. Blocking apps, scheduled blocks, breaks and allowances, application passwords and 'All locking features' require Pro.
accountRequired: No account is mentioned for the free download. Pro is unlocked with a product key bought through Paddle, and Cold Turkey keeps your email and purchase details.
privacyNotes: The privacy policy says: 'We do not collect your app settings, web history, search history or which websites and apps were blocked.' The browser extension needs permission to read and change all web pages in order to enforce blocks. Usage data used to calculate breaks 'is never sent off your device'.
limitations: Windows and macOS only: 'Linux, ChromeOS, Android, iOS or other operating systems are not supported.'
The most useful features (scheduled blocks, app blocking, locking) require the paid Pro version
Deliberately hard to undo. The site says it 'makes it almost impossible to stop the block once you lock it. No, you can't just uninstall it.' This can backfire if you set it up wrongly.

name: Super Productivity
maker: Johannes Millan and open-source contributors (super-productivity on GitHub)
purpose: A free, open-source to-do list with built-in time tracking, a Pomodoro timer and a focus mode that keeps your data on your own device.
keyFeatures: Tasks, subtasks, projects and repeating tasks in lists, Kanban or an Eisenhower Matrix
Built-in time tracking with history and exportable work logs
Focus mode, Pomodoro timer and breaks
Calendar timeboxing and GitHub, GitLab and Jira integrations
Optional sync through SuperSync, WebDAV or Dropbox
costDetail: 100% free under the MIT licence. The pricing page says 'There are no premium app tiers, hidden app costs, or paid app features.' Development is supported by optional GitHub Sponsors donations. The optional SuperSync cloud sync service 'is currently provided free of charge', but its terms reserve the right to introduce fees in the future and require an account. WebDAV and Dropbox sync are alternatives.
accountRequired: No ('No account needed · Works offline'). An account is only needed if you choose the SuperSync sync service.
privacyNotes: 'Your tasks stay on your device by default.' The pricing FAQ says: 'We do not run analytics inside the app, require logins, or sell usage data.' The iOS App Store privacy label says 'Data Not Collected'.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard shortcuts for capturing ideas, switching tasks and navigating, and selectable themes. Recent App Store release notes mention 'Improved accessible names, keyboard controls, and task focus behavior', but the App Store accessibility section says the developer has not indicated supported features. No formal accessibility statement was found.
limitations: It is a task and time-tracking tool. The official site does not describe any app or website blocking.
Syncing between devices needs setup (a SuperSync account, WebDAV or Dropbox), and SuperSync may start charging in future
Volunteer-maintained, with community support (GitHub, Reddit) rather than a support team

Block in fixed time periods, after a time limit (e.g. 10 minutes per hour), or both

limitations: Browser-only. It does not block phone or computer apps, and there is no Safari version (the site points macOS and iOS users to ivBlock, a separate product).

name: f.lux
purpose: Makes your computer screen warmer at night and like daylight during the day, to cut late-night blue glare.
keyFeatures: Automatically shifts screen colour with the time of day, based on your location
Bedtime timing with a wake-time setting
Settings for the type of lighting in your room
Optional control of compatible home lighting (personal edition)

privacyNotes: Uses online mapping services, including Google Maps, to find your location 'usually just once when you set things up' so it can work out sunrise and sunset. Daily automatic update checks send some information about your computer configuration, and it collects which versions and features are used.
limitations: No official iPhone, iPad or regular Android app. iOS needs a jailbroken device, and the Android build was a 2016 'preview for rooted devices'.
Company or managed use needs the paid Corporate Edition or your employer's permission
The FAQ lists display-driver conflicts, e.g. 'My Windows 10 computer flickers at sunset. Disable Windows Night Light.'

Premium: built-in authenticator codes (TOTP), vault health reports and alerts, file attachments, emergency access
costDetail: The Free plan ('Always free') covers unlimited passwords on unlimited devices, passkeys, the generator, encrypted export, Bitwarden Send and sharing with one other user. Premium costs US$19.80 per year (shown as US$1.65/month billed annually; taxes not included) and adds an integrated authenticator (TOTP), 5 GB of file attachments, emergency access and vault health reports and alerts. Families costs US$47.88 per year (US$3.99/month) for up to 6 users. The current Premium price was announced on 21 January 2026. Core password management is free, so essential features do not need payment.
licence: GPL-3.0 (apps/clients) and AGPL-3.0 (server); some code under the separate Bitwarden License v1.0
accountRequired: Yes. You create a free Bitwarden account to hold your encrypted vault. You can also run the Bitwarden server yourself (self-hosting).
privacyNotes: The App Store listing describes 'an end-to-end encrypted password vault that only you can access', and the pricing page lists 'Zero-knowledge encryption'. The Chrome Web Store disclosure says it handles personally identifiable and authentication information and does not sell data to third parties.
accessibilityNotes: Bitwarden's contributor documentation says 'Bitwarden strives to comply with WCAG AA requirements' and covers keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. The App Store accessibility section says the developer has not indicated supported features, and no formal accessibility conformance report (VPAT) was found.
limitations: Premium extras such as built-in 2FA codes and vault health reports now cost US$19.80 per year
Free sharing is limited to one other Bitwarden user
The F-Droid Android build has no push notifications, so vault sync is manual

name: Privacy Badger
purpose: A free browser extension from the digital-rights nonprofit EFF that automatically learns to block hidden trackers that follow you across websites.
keyFeatures: Learns to block third-party trackers by their behaviour, not from a fixed blocklist
Sends Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track signals
Can replace tracking social media widgets (e.g. Like buttons) with click-to-activate placeholders
Red, yellow and green sliders to adjust blocking per domain
costDetail: Free: 'a free browser extension made by the leading digital rights nonprofit EFF'. The Safari version is listed as Free on the Mac App Store. Optional donations support EFF. The source code is under GPLv3+.
privacyNotes: 'Privacy Badger will never share data about your browsing unless you choose to share it (by filing a broken site report).' It needs access to all sites to detect trackers, and it checks EFF's CDN for updates ('EFF does not set cookies or retain IP addresses for these queries'). The Mac App Store label says 'Data Not Collected'.
accessibilityNotes: The Mac App Store listing says the developer has not indicated supported accessibility features. No official accessibility statement was found.
limitations: It is not a full ad blocker. It doesn't block all ads, for example ads on YouTube itself, which uses no third-party trackers.
Safari support is Mac-only (Safari 26.5+, macOS 15.7.7 or later). EFF says 'We are working towards Safari on iOS support.'
On Android it only works in Firefox for Android or Edge for Android, because Chrome on Android does not support extensions

name: Have I Been Pwned
purpose: A website where you can check for free whether your email address has appeared in known data breaches, and sign up for alerts about future breaches.
keyFeatures: Free email address breach search in your browser
Free Notify Me email alerts when your address appears in new breaches
Pwned Passwords: check whether a password has appeared in breaches, using k-anonymity
Domain monitoring (free up to 10 breached addresses; larger domains need a subscription)
Paid API plans for apps and organisations
costDetail: Free for individuals. The Free tier lists 'Browser email search, Email notifications, Pwned Passwords, Breach monitoring API, Monitor domains with up to 10 breached addresses'. Paid subscriptions are for API email search and larger domains: Core from US$4.39/month paid annually (Core 1: 'billed as $52.68/y'), Pro from US$379/month paid annually, High RPM from US$1,150/month paid annually. Amounts are in US dollars per the Terms of Use. The essential personal check (search your email, get alerts) is free.
accountRequired: No for a one-off email or password check. Notify Me requires verifying your email address. Domain search requires signing in to the dashboard and proving you own or control the domain.
privacyNotes: Privacy policy: 'We do not collect or store your personal information when you conduct a search in the HIBP database.' Web server logs are kept for up to 31 days and may include your IP address. Pwned Passwords sends only the first 5 characters of the password's SHA-1 hash (k-anonymity).
limitations: It only knows about breaches loaded into HIBP. A 'not found' result doesn't prove an account or password is safe.
It won't tell you which password was leaked for your email address
API email search and monitoring of larger domains require a paid subscription
